where: Section 1, first bullet defining a fiducial marker
problem: "a black square with a white border and an inner code" reads as if the white ring is the border of the pattern. In standard markers (ArUco/ARToolKit style) the thick black square ring is itself the border that gives the edges, the ID code sits inside that ring, and the white margin outside the ring is only a quiet zone for detection. A student can picture the layers in the wrong order.
fix: "A fiducial marker is a printed pattern: a thick black square ring (the border) around a small binary code, printed on a white background. The ring gives strong edges; the code gives an ID so several markers can coexist; the white margin outside the ring keeps the edges clean."

problem: The depth formula Z = f × W ÷ w is stated without its assumption: it holds when the marker face is parallel to the image plane. For a tilted marker the apparent width w shrinks by roughly cos of the tilt angle, so a student applying the formula to a slanted marker gets a distance that is too large.
fix: Add one line after the formula: "This holds when the marker face is parallel to the image plane. A tilted marker looks narrower, so full pose comes from the homography, not from this one-line size formula."

where: Section 1, bullet "Decompose H with camera intrinsics into pose R, t"
problem: Homography decomposition does not give a single pose. For a planar target the maths returns two candidate (R, t) solutions, and the tracker must pick one. Without this, a student wonders why the same marker sometimes flips or jumps.
fix: "Decompose H with camera intrinsics into pose R, t. The decomposition gives two candidate solutions; keep the one where the marker lies in front of the camera (positive depth) and is consistent with the previous frame."
